recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No current FHIR source edit is needed for FHIR-17046 unless a future work group decision revisits the broader rules for slicing polymorphic elements.
issue_request: FHIR-17046 was Published/Persuasive for the STU3 FHIR-core profiling page and requested removing the sentence "This technique can also be used on elements that do not repeat, but that have a choice of data types" from the slicing introduction.
initial_application: The issue was applied by commit d06bf2327778312bc00babdae00b424e81fc1d78, whose message is "GF#17046 - fix definition" and whose git-svn id records svn revision 14318, matching the Jira application comments. That commit deleted exactly the requested sentence from source/profiling.html.
additional_context: The removed sentence had been introduced by FHIR-8606 to clarify slicing of non-repeating choice elements. Current source/profiling.html no longer contains that sentence, and the current profiling text separately supports polymorphic discriminator paths with ofType(). The page remains part of current source navigation through source/documentation.html, and no relevant Zulip or Confluence records were found.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. Exact git-grep verification showed the sentence is absent from HEAD source/profiling.html and present in the parent of the FHIR-17046 application commit.
